newsitem.title: ITALY: Bergamo-Orio plans expansion after traffic growth.
newsitem.headline: Bergamo-Orio plans expansion after traffic growth.

text.p: Bergamo-Orio aiport is poised for further expansion after an increase in traffic last year, its managing company SACBO said.
Airlines using Bergamo-Orio made better use of their cargo capacity in 1996 resulting in an overall 16 percent increase in tonnage moved through the airport.

"In 1996 we invested more than 20 billion lire in infrastructure and equipment. But the Orio airport needs another 100 billion lire of investment to be fully operative. This sum has already been programmed but SACBO's directors must approve it," SACBO director Giorgio Tattoni said in a statement.
Cargo movement last year rose 27 percent to 4,560 tonnes. The number of commercial landings rose five percent to 7,676.

The new investment is for a new cargo area planned for north of the runway which in terms of Italian cargo movements ranks fourth behind Rome's Fiumicino and Milan's Linate and Malpensa airports. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
